experiment: Quake 1.06 demo1 timedemo, real A/B of two binaries (ABBA quartets)

protocol.contrast_estimator: per quartet (A + A - B - B) / 2 on log values
protocol.interval: percentile bootstrap over the 8 quartet differences, 10000 resamples

binaries.difference: arm B adds the BT/BTS/BTR/BTC register form, SETcc and SAHF to the dynamic core

detection_floor.basis: A/A placebo quartet dispersion on this host
detection_floor.note: a real A/B on this host needs at least this many quartets per arm to resolve the effect; the A/A estimate itself may be optimistic if host noise is autocorrelated

independent_replication.note: an earlier A/B of the same code change on the same node, run before the comment-only source cleanup; only its summary numbers were kept

fallback_accounting.instrumentation: local patch, not part of the branch; counts interpreter entries by guest CS:EIP
fallback_accounting.timedemo: demo1, 969 frames, same node and configuration for both builds

correctness_gate.test: bit_test_semantics.asm, 19 cases, interpreter core vs dynamic core

limitations: one node only: the effect size and the detection floor are node properties

the measured effect exceeds the 1.19 percent fallback-window estimate because the earlier attribution counted interpreter samples but not the block teardown and re-translation cost that every fallback also causes
SAHF still costs one C helper call per execution
BT with a memory bit base still falls back to the interpreter by design
artifact_role: registry evidence for the closure of the decoder gap; the same artifact is published in kaaburgh/dosbox-staging PR #13
